_doc: Per-building curation applied on top of LiDAR+OSM. Keyed by OSM element id (way/relation) or by name. Fields: wall/roof {colour, material}; zones: facade split along the footprint's long axis (from/to are fractions 0..1, measured from end 'origin': west|east|north|south); crown: facade band at the top {height, colour, material, sign_colour, tip: only the first fraction of the long axis from the origin end}; min_part_height: apply only to parts taller than this; label {name, en, kind, height, year, rebuilt, by, building} as in landmarks.LABELS; sources. Materials: wall, glass, concrete, metal, pkin, bronze_grid, sign. Areas (any OSM area id, e.g. a stadium): stripes {colours, width (m along the perimeter), material, min_height} paint the walls of every building part inside it in vertical bands by angle around the area's centre; stripes.bands [{to (m above ground), colour | checker [two colours] + cell [w, h m] + p/dp (share of the second colour, rising with height), material}] paint by height instead, or {to, repeat [[m, colour, material], ...]} cycled floor by floor; smooth {masts, mast_h, outline, podium} rebuilds a stadium roof as one surface (median height by distance from the smoothed outer edge) with thin masts round the rim. (Amsterdam's entries; scripts/overrides.json holds Warsaw's.) year: the construction year for the year slider (zones.py), where BAG's is a restoration's or missing.

99203577.name: Westertoren (1638, Hendrick de Keyser; 85 m)
99203577._note: square brick and sandstone base; octagonal sandstone stage; lead-clad timber stages; Maximilian's blue imperial crown with gold at the top

Westerkerk._note: BAG year 1990 is a restoration; the church is 1620-31 red brick with sandstone dressings

114120359.name: Zuiderkerk (1611; tower 1614)
114120359._note: brick body and tower base, white sandstone stage with clock, dark lead spire (photo: stone stage #79726c in shade, spire #434a5c)

57862728.name: Munttoren (base 1490, top 1620)
57862728._note: red brick base of the medieval gate, light sandstone and timber octagon, lead spire

57857592.name: Oude Kerk
57857592._note: weathered brown brick, sandstone tower stage, lead-clad timber spire; lead roofs (photo roofs #87919f)

220749328.name: Nieuwe Kerk
220749328._note: buff sandstone and yellowish brick (photo #9c7b50 at dusk); blue-grey slate roofs come from the ortho

431070185.name: Rijksmuseum (1885, Pierre Cuypers)
431070185._note: red brick with cream sandstone bands floor by floor; slate roofs from the ortho

57856845.name: Amsterdam Centraal (1889, Cuypers and Van Gendt)
57856845._note: red brick with cream stone bands (photo mix #956a5a); the outline takes in the whole platform area, so a plain wall colour rather than area-wide bands

Beurs van Berlage._note: Berlage's plain red-orange brick (photo, sunlit side)

57856769.name: NEMO (1997, Renzo Piano)
57856769._note: pre-oxidised green copper cladding; the sloping roof is a public stone-paved square (ortho)

269000174.name: Koninklijk Theater Carré (1887)
269000174._note: cream stucco classical front on the Amstel

451533145.name: Zuidkap
451533145._note: the train sheds: iron and glass arches
